summary: Multiple lines of evidence indicate that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalisations in patients with HFpEF. A nationwide cohort study found SGLT2 inhibitors lowered the risk of hospital admission for heart failure among patients with type 2 diabetes and HFpEF [1]. A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs reported that SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced the risk of heart failure hospitalisations over the long term (≥1 year) [2]. Another meta-analysis of 15 RCTs specifically in HFpEF patients showed treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors reduced hospitalisation for heart failure [4]. Additionally, a prespecified pooled analysis of DELIVER and EMPEROR-preserved trials demonstrated a reduction in the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalisation, with a 27% risk reduction in the broad high-risk subgroup (hospitalisation within 12 months) [5]. These findings consistently support a beneficial effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on reducing HF hospitalisations in HFpEF.
evidence_gaps: The papers do not fully address whether the reduction in hospitalisation is consistent across all HFpEF phenotypes or etiologies, nor do they provide detailed data on long-term outcomes beyond the studied follow-up periods in relation to specific subtypes of HFpEF.
